title: Convergent Evolution: How Different Language Models Learn Similar Number Representations
abstract: arXiv:2604.20817v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Language models trained on natural text learn to represent numbers using periodic features with dominant periods at $T=2, 5, 10$. In this paper, we identify a two-tiered hierarchy of these features: while Transformers, Linear RNNs, LSTMs, and classical word embeddings trained in different ways all learn features that have period-$T$ spikes in the Fourier domain, only some learn geometrically separable features that can be used to linearly classify a number mod-$T$. To explain this incongruity, we prove that Fourier domain sparsity is necessary but not sufficient for mod-$T$ geometric separability. Empirically, we investigate when model training yields geometrically separable features, finding that the data, architecture, optimizer, and tokenizer all play key roles. translated_title: 趋同演化：不同语言模型如何学习相似的数值表示
translated_abstract: 在自然文本上训练的语言模型学会使用周期性特征来表示数字，这些特征的主导周期为$T=2, 5, 10$。在本文中，我们识别了这些特征的两层层级结构：虽然以不同方式训练的Transformer、线性RNN、LSTM和经典词嵌入都能在傅里叶域中学习到具有周期$T$尖峰的特征，但只有部分模型能学习到几何可分离的特征，这些特征可用于线性分类数字的模$T$。为了解释这种不一致性，我们证明了傅里叶域稀疏性是模$T$几何可分离性的必要但不充分条件。在实证上，我们调查了何时模型训练能产生几何可分离的特征，发现数据、架构、优化器和分词器都起关键作用。特别是，我们识别了模型获取几何可分离特征的两种不同途径：它们可以从互补共现中学习这些特征。
tldr: 本文揭示了不同语言模型在表示数字时存在趋同的周期性特征，并证明了傅里叶稀疏性是模$T$几何可分离性的必要非充分条件，同时识别了数据、架构等因素如何影响模型获取可分离特征。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals convergent periodic features in number representations across different language models, proving Fourier sparsity is necessary but not sufficient for mod-$T$ geometric separability, and identifies key factors influencing the acquisition of separable features.
